description: THE PROFILE-GATE BOUNDARY, now fully retired (issue #742, reversed by ruling #833 via issues #838 and #841). Byte-for-byte the same source as `heritage-alias-redefinition-rejected-when-active`, checked under Core alone -- and now producing the SAME thirteen `ol-reserved-word` diagnostics, because `spec/grammar.md:408` makes every profile's names built in whether or not the profile is claimed and `:414` makes every alias spelling a built-in name. HISTORY, and why the file name is now false: it was written to prove `ol-reserved-word`'s primitive category was profile-gated, so it expected ZERO diagnostics; #838 then blocked the nine turtle aliases `fd`/`bk`/`lt`/`rt`/`st`/`ht`/`pu`/`pd`/`cs` it had measured, leaving it at nine; the last four -- `pr`/`bf`/`bl`/`se`, which resolve to the CORE canonicals `print`/`butfirst`/`butlast`/`sentence` -- went through the profile-gated branch that #841 deleted, taking the count to thirteen. Nothing in this program is "legal in core" any more. The name is kept anyway: renaming the six inverted fixtures belongs to the corpus sweep in issue #842, and keeping the source byte-identical to its sibling is what removes the possibility that the two drift. The DIFFERENCE between this fixture and that sibling was exactly the size of the remaining gate; it is now empty, which is the strongest statement the pair can make. `"check": true` for the same reason as the sibling: a checker rule with no execution. `message` is deliberately absent from the diagnostics below, and the asymmetry with the twin is intentional rather than an oversight: the harness does not compare `message` even when a fixture supplies it (measured -- a deliberately wrong `message` here still passed the suite), so including it would add an assertion nothing verifies. Diagnostic identity is `code` plus `params` and "prose is presentation" (`spec/error-model.md:253`); the learner-facing wording is pinned by unit tests instead. Dropping the decorative `message` from the twins is a corpus-wide edit and belongs to issue #842.
